reasons: Classification is correct: § 2.1 imposes a three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay expressly 'without reduction or termination rights', which is the rule's stated walk-away position and fails the fallback on every material term (single 12-month commitment, 30-day reduction right, true-up not penalty).

The redline lands precisely on the playbook fallback: commitment confined to the current twelve-month term, reducible/terminable on 30 days' written notice, and shortfall converted to a true-up with penalties, liquidated damages and accelerated fees expressly excluded.

The high changed-character ratio (0.788) is justified here — the original sentence is a single take-or-pay covenant whose duration, reduction right and remedy all had to be replaced; narrowing rather than deleting is the least disruptive route given the deal's committed-spend structure, and deletion is offered as the preferred alternative.

Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, correctly notes the conflict with § 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement, states what changed and why, and offers the fallback/alternative without lecturing.
No double-flagging or party-direction error: the commitment runs against Customer (our party), and the edit does not disadvantage us.
